key_insight: Multi-Head LatentMoE + Head Parallel gives a deterministic, communication-efficient way to run sparse Mixture-of-Experts so communication no longer scales linearly with the number of activated experts and data-dependent metadata is eliminated.
problem_solved: Reduces EP-style MoE training costs by addressing communication blowup with k, load imbalance related latency/memory spikes, and costly data-dependent metadata exchange.
method: Multi-Head LatentMoE: use a multi-head latent routing/gating scheme to deterministically map tokens to expert groups, decoupling communication volume from the number of activated experts.
Head Parallel: partition computation across attention heads (or head-aligned expert shards) to enable deterministic, evenly distributed work and memory, avoiding load imbalance.
Eliminate data-dependent routing metadata by deriving routing deterministically from model structure and heads, enabling fixed communication patterns and simpler all-to-all schedules.
impact: Makes large-scale sparse MoE training faster, more memory-efficient and easier to implement/debug — lowering infrastructure cost and enabling more predictable scaling for practitioners.
visual_elements: Block diagram comparing Expert Parallel vs Multi-Head LatentMoE + Head Parallel showing deterministic routing and reduced all-to-all connections
Bar/line chart: communication bytes (y) vs activated experts k (x) showing linear growth for EP and flat/sublinear for the proposed method
Heatmap of expert load across tokens for EP (imbalanced) vs Head Parallel (balanced), illustrating improved load distribution
Pipeline illustration showing elimination of metadata exchange (crossed-out metadata icon) and fixed communication steps
paper_title: Multi-Head LatentMoE and Head Parallel: Communication-Efficient and Deterministic MoE Parallelism
paper_authors: Chenwei Cui, Rockwell Jackson, Benjamin Joseph Herrera, Ana María Tárano, Hannah Kerner
